464.t: Touring Japan in 1966, with Herbie Mann and the drum tour
464.s: He first went to Japan in 1966 with Herbie Mann, then on a drum tour with Blakey, Elvin Jones, Tony Williams and others. The tour ended early after drug arrests.
464.q: They did. I can go back to 1966 with Herbie Mann, and then I went back to Japan a little later in that year with a special drum tour that had Art Blakey, Elvin Jones, Tony Williams, McCoy Tyner, Ben Tucker played bass, Wayne Shorter and myself. It was fantastic, but it was a very bad tour in that…

464.t: Japan 1966: first passport and the drum tour arrests
464.s: He tours Japan with Herbie Mann and then a drummers' tour where Tony Williams and Elvin Jones were jailed on narcotics charges and Kenny Clarke was deported.
464.ch: Marshall Brown, Ellington and first trips abroad
464.q: I think so. Then I wound up going to Japan twice before I even went to Europe. It was very interesting. I went again later on in 1966 with a drum tour. It was Tony Williams, Elvin Jones, Art Blakey, McCoy Tyner, Ben Tucker on bass, Wayne Shorter and myself. We played for about a week and Tony…

89.s: He calls South America sensational and says they played Shepherd's Hotel in Cairo for two weeks in 1927, but visited North Africa only in 1964.
89.ch: Europe and South America with Sam Wooding
89.q: Yes, we played the Shepherd's Hotel in Cairo, Egypt, in '27. We had a two-week engagement, two weeks.

89.t: South American tour from Marseilles to Buenos Aires
89.s: After Europe they sailed to Buenos Aires and played vaudeville theaters and cabarets in Argentina and Uruguay for six months.
89.ch: Europe and South America with Sam Wooding
89.q: from Europe to -- we went from Marseilles to Buenos Aires and we stayed in South America for about six months. There we played Buenos Aires, Montevideo, Rosario, Tucumán, and one other town -- we played vaudeville and we also played cabaret. We played theaters there and cabarets. We played at the…

111.t: Tony Williams's marijuana and Elvin's arrest
111.s: Elvin tells that Tony Williams gave the police his name and he was arrested in Hokkaido, and Keiko saw him handcuffed.
111.q: He (Tony Williams) was a drug user cause he got caught with, he had some marijuana. I said, “What are you doing?” Cause he’s out there smoking it on the train and everything. I said, I told him, I said, “You know what you better do is flush it down the toilet. That’s the best thing to do cause…

372.t: The 1965 European tour with Bill Evans and Herb Ellis story
372.s: Konitz recalls Evans's drug trouble, the split trios, and a story about 'Detour Ahead'.
372.q: At that point I thought he did. Then I realized that [it] was too difficult for him to move around even with his boys. Later on we did that European tour where Lennie played either with the Connie Kay duo, or solo, and I was playing with Bill Evans.

64.t: The Haiti tour and the conga of Ti Rurale
64.s: He toured Haiti with Bud Johnson and Kenny Dorham, and met the drummer Ti Rurale; he also confirms the Stravinsky ballet music in Seven Lively Arts.
64.ch: Sideman years and the European tour
64.q: Kenny Dorum, a wonderful trumpet player. That was a fascinating group because it was Charlie Smith, Lloyd Trotman on bass, John Collins on guitar, myself on piano and the horns I mentioned. We spent a month in Haiti. We went down to play at a festival and after the festival was over we played in…

219.s: Wein recounts Buddy Rich, Louie Bellson and others, then Elvin and Tony Williams, jailed on Japan tours.
219.q: Well, you feel badly for the Japanese promoters, but you still have buddies (Rich and Louie Belson and Philly Jo, and Charlie Persip) who are in jail. And you go to the Japanese jail and you say, "Why can't you let these guys out on bail? You're hurting your own thing. They pay bail and come back…

406.t: A second Miami Cotton Club show and the 1959 revue in Brazil
406.s: Another Cotton Club show in Miami lasted briefly. In 1959 he was music director of a revue that played Rio, Brazil, Buenos Aires and Montevideo with local musicians; the Belo Horizonte show was cut off by a revolution.
406.ch: Streetcar, Cab revival shows and trips abroad
406.q: Miami for Cab, another Cotton Club show. Some other guys got an idea to put on a Cotton Club show like they did before because that one was such a hit, but it didn't last too long, although they were still using Benny Davis and the music.

614.t: State Department tour of South America in 1958
614.s: A three-and-a-half-month tour in which the State Department used the band poorly, sometimes giving one concert a week.
614.q: For the State Department, yes. And it was an interesting tour. However, unfortunately our State Department people, at least during that period, were not very well equipped to get the most good out of having someone like

381.t: Touring South America with Cab and leading a band there in 1954
381.s: Hinton recalls the 1951 Montevideo tour with Cab; Francis took a sextet back in 1954 and became the featured band.
381.q: In 1951, because I took a band down there -- for some reason, in South America, which is a rhythmic country --- all those countries are rhythmic down there, and so the drummer is the star.

92.t: Touring Haiti with Budd Johnson and Billy Taylor
92.s: Six weeks in Haiti with Johnson, Taylor, Lloyd Trotman, Charlie Smith and Kenny Dorham, living in a mountain town with voodoo drums at night.
92.ch: Haiti, Artie Shaw and Los Angeles work
